page.layout: One page of text in a single column of short annotated entries, set in roman and italic with some Greek. No marginal notes or separate blocks are printed. Page number at the top left, running head at the top centre, catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: hæresies, lib.1.tom. 1. Interpretari possest Samaritas custodes propterea quod custodum locum in terra obtinebant: aut quod custodes essent constituti secundum legem Mosi. Eucherius pag. 185. Samaritæ custodes, eo quod a Babylonis illic ad custodiam collocati essent ludæorum. Ceterum Samar verbum est Ebraicum, non Assyrium. Assyrij & Chaldæi pro eo Natarii ufurpant. Vnde in ea lingua custodes potius Natarita dicerentur.

Ex quibus plerique divinas cæremonias receperunt, reliquis in errore gentilitatis perseverantibus] hæc ita restituit possent ad veritatem historiæ, qui divinas cæremonias receperunt, & simul in errore gentilitatis perseverarunt. Nam cum Dominum colerent (verba sunt interpretis antiqui, 4. Reg. 17.33.) diis quoque suis serviebant juxta consuetudinem gentium, de quibus translati fuerant Samariam. His adde quod in eodem capite verf. 41. Fuerunt igitur gentes isti timentes quidem Dominum, sed nihilominus & idolis suis servientes: nam & filii eorum & nepotes sicut fecerunt patres sui, ita faciunt usque in hodiernum diem.
Divinas cæremonias] lege præceptas, quam solam recipiebant, rejectis prophetis & hagiographis.

Achas] cum in libris Græcorum fit ἀχάζ, putarim Sulpicium scripsisse Achaz: tamen non adversus eam consuetudinem quam notavi Observat lib.IX cap.IX. Sic in hoc libro reperies Ioachas, qui est obliquus a recto Ioachas. Sic ἰωάχ pro ἰωάχ legitur apud Iosephum, & alibi Iosæs pro Iosephi. Quod tamen & aliam rationem habet. Nam etiam Iose dicimus, unde potest esse Iosæs, ut ex Iesu factum Iesus, Græca & Latina declinatione.
Deos gentium] Moloch 4. Reg. 16.3. Baalim 2. Paralip 28. 2. & Deos Dammasci sive Darmasci, 4. Reg. 28.23.
Piaculo] id est, crimine. Proprie crimen ob quod expiatio fieri debet.

Ezechias] rectius scribitur Ezecias. Primum quia Græci sic scribunt Ἑζεκίας: deinde quia est Coph in Ebræo characterere, quam consonantem antiqui expresserunt semper per C, simplex. Vide Alphabetum nostrum vetus.

page.notes: Greek words in the "Achas" and "Ioachas" entries are copied from a faint scan and are doubtful: ἀχάζ, ἰωάχ and Ἑζεκίας are marked as uncertain where the letters did not resolve, and the Greek of the Iosephum line is uncertain. Many lemmas run into the text with a bracket; the bracket is printed, so it is kept. Show-through from the reverse page appears at the left and right edges and is omitted. Some words in the first entry, especially "Eucherius pag. 185", "Ceterum" and "Natarita", are only partly legible on the scan and may contain printing errors, and the line "Divinas cæremonias" is set in a single block with an unclear lemma. Some of the fine detail of the left-margin lemma list could not be resolved and is transcribed as the most likely reading.
